newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil closes sharply up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil closes sharply up but off highs.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Bullish sentiment, boosted by strong gains in Chicago soyoil and technical buying pushed up prices sharply higher. But some profit-taking were seen and prices closed off highs. Firm fundamentals also aided prices. March broke 1,300 ringgit and next resistance is 1,320.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL -Firmer prices were seen due to refiners' buying and interest confined to nearby CPOs and products.
Soyoil firmed on bullish data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture and heavy fund buying.

Some Malaysian traders have earlier estimated production in December to fall by 16 to 18 percent over November, while several Malaysian plantations projected palm oil output in December to fall by up to 15 percent against a month ago.
"The further drop in output for December is expected as it was mainly because of seasonal down trend and unfavourable weather conditions," an official of a plantation house said.
The largest drop came mainly from the East Malaysian state of Sabah, a trader said.
Ivan Wong, a crop forecaster will release his latest December crop data on January 14 before the announcement of official key December data on January 15
Traders had earlier projected end-December stocks at 805,000 tonnes against end-November's 955,965 tonnes.
Exports in December were estimated at between 660,000 and 680,000 tonnes, against PORLA's 632,441 tonnes in November.
Traders said technically, there was a strong buying spree when third month March futures rose above the 1,300 ringgit.
It rose to a high of 1,317 ringgit before falling to close at 1,300 ringgit ($528.45) a tonne, up 28 ringgit from Friday.
Spot January futures closed 28 ringgit up at 1,345 ringgit a tonne and February futures month was up 33 at 1,323.
Physical Jan (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,350 against bids at 1,345 after trading from 1,340 to 1,355 .

Jan (central) was offered at 1,350 and bids at 1,340 with trades of 1,335 to 1,355. Jan (north) was bid at 1,345 and 1,335. Feb (south) saw offers at 1,350 with bids at 1,345 with earlier trades of 1,340 to 1,355, and Feb (central) was offered at 1,350 and bids at 1,340.
